c.tagline: Hokkaido's historic port of harbor-hill night views and morning-market seafood.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing is very limited here; the GO taxi app can sometimes find a cab in the center, but most rides are hailed on the street or booked by phone. Fares are metered, and many taxis now take cards and IC cards.

emergency.note: 119 reaches fire and ambulance; 110 is police. English-speaking operators are limited, so having your location written in Japanese helps.

hood_desc: The historic hillside quarter climbing the slopes below Mount Hakodate, with its famous Hachiman-zaka slope, the Orthodox, Catholic and Anglican churches, Western-style former consulates and the ropeway to the night-view summit; the most scenic and atmospheric place to stay.

The waterfront district of the Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses, now full of shops, cafes and restaurants, with harbor promenades and easy tram access; a lively, walkable base between Motomachi and the station.

The central area around JR Hakodate Station and the Asaichi morning market, the city's transport hub and the spot for a fresh seafood and uni breakfast; the most convenient base for onward trains, trams and buses.

The neighborhood around the star-shaped Goryokaku fort and its viewing tower, a cherry-blossom park in spring, ringed by the city's everyday shops and dining; a quieter, more local base away from the tourist waterfront.
The seaside hot-spring resort district on the eastern edge of the city near the airport, lined with onsen ryokan and hotels with mineral baths; best for travelers who want to soak and unwind.

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: Trams and city buses run from around 6:00 AM to roughly 10:30-11:00 PM; there is no late-night service, so taxis fill the gap after the last tram.
transit.note: Hakodate's compact old-fashioned streetcar (tram) system runs two lines linking the station, the bay, Motomachi and Yunokawa Onsen, backed up by an extensive Hakodate Bus network; the trams are the easiest way to reach the main sights.
transit.pay: Tap on with a national IC card such as Suica, Kitaca or ICOCA, or pay the driver in cash; a one-day tram-and-bus pass is good value if you plan several rides.

bus: Highway coaches to Sapporo and southern Hokkaido

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to JR Hakodate Station (~20 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; polite, high-quality service is standard and already included.

food.name: Morning-market squid (ika)
food.desc: Hakodate's signature: ultra-fresh squid served as translucent ika-somen noodles, or caught live yourself at the market's squid-fishing tank.

places.name: Ganso Katsu Ika Tsuribori
places.note: Fish your own live squid from the tank and it is sliced sashimi-style on the spot; opens 6am.

places.name: Donburi Yokocho Ichiba
places.note: Alley of tiny family stalls doing ika-somen and grilled squid from the dawn auction.

places.name: Hakodate Asaichi outer stalls
places.note: Cheapest way to try squid straight off the boats; most stalls wind down by early afternoon.

food.name: Hakodate shio ramen
food.desc: The clear salt-based ramen that Hakodate gave Japan: pale kelp-and-pork broth, straight thin noodles, often finished with Hokkaido butter.

places.name: Ajisai Honten
places.note: The city's most famous shio ramen shop and the benchmark bowl locals send visitors to.

places.name: Menchubo Ajisai Bay Area
places.note: Same kitchen, handier for sightseers around the red-brick warehouses.

places.name: Ramen Kamome
places.note: Long-running neighbourhood shop for a quieter, less queued bowl of classic shio.

food.name: Kaisen-don (seafood rice bowl)
food.desc: A lacquer bowl of vinegared rice buried under crab, scallop, salmon roe, squid and uni, chosen topping by topping at the morning market.

places.name: Kikuyo Shokudo Honten
places.note: Since 1956; the tomoe-don of uni, scallop and salmon roe is the classic order.

places.name: Donburi Yokocho Ichiba
places.note: Dozens of donburi counters side by side, so you can build a bowl to your own budget.

places.name: Hakodate Asaichi Ekini Market
places.note: Indoor market hall with seated donburi counters, useful in bad weather.

food.name: Nama uni (raw sea urchin)
food.desc: Southern Hokkaido bafun and murasaki urchin served plain on rice or in the shell; sweet, briny and at its peak from June to August.

places.name: Uni Murakami Hakodate Honten
places.note: Specialist known for additive-free uni that tastes of sea rather than preservative.

places.name: Kikuyo Shokudo Honten
places.note: Reliable uni-don at market prices with the roe graded in front of you.

places.name: Hakodate Morning Market seafood stalls
places.note: Several stalls crack urchins to order for a quick standing snack.

food.name: Hakodate cheese omelette
food.desc: A wobbly, half-baked cheesecake-souffle in a foil cup, invented in Hakodate and now the city's best-loved edible souvenir.

places.name: Snaffle's Kanemori Factory
places.area: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses, Bay Area
places.note: The originator's flagship, with the cakes baked and boxed on site.

places.name: Snaffle's Hakodate Station shop
places.note: Handiest branch for picking up a chilled box on the way to the train.

places.name: Petite Merveille
places.note: Local rival doing the Mel Cheese version, softer and more custardy.

food.name: Lucky Pierrot Chinese chicken burger
food.desc: Hakodate's cult local burger chain: sweet-sour fried chicken in a bun, made only here and voted Japan's best local burger.

places.name: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Honten
places.note: The original 1987 branch, wildly decorated and the one most visitors queue at.

places.name: Lucky Pierrot Hakodate Ekimae
places.note: Convenient branch for a burger between trains; same menu, shorter wait.

places.name: Lucky Pierrot Goryokaku Koen-mae
places.note: Roomier tables, good stop after the star-fort park.

food.name: Hakodate Beer (ji-biru)
food.desc: Locally brewed lager, alt and weizen made with Hakodate's soft water, poured metres from the harbour it is named after.

places.name: Hakodate Beer Hall
places.note: Brewpub in a brick warehouse with tanks on view and Hokkaido seafood to match.

places.name: Hakodate Beer Hall Kanemori
places.note: Beer garden atmosphere right on the bay, good at sunset before the ropeway.

places.name: Bay Area izakaya strip
places.note: Most local izakaya keep at least one Hakodate Beer tap alongside Sapporo.

food.name: Hokkaido milk and soft-serve drinks
food.desc: Hokkaido's rich dairy turned into cold bottled milk, milkshakes and melting soft-serve floats; a Hakodate market ritual after breakfast.

places.name: Milkissimo
places.note: Hokkaido milk gelato and shakes made with local dairy, right on the waterfront.

places.name: Hakodate Morning Market dairy stands
places.note: Bottled Hokkaido milk and drinking yoghurt sold beside the seafood counters.

places.name: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Honten
places.note: Thick Hokkaido milkshakes that locals order with the Chinese chicken burger.

landmarks: Mount Hakodate Night View
Ride the ropeway to this 334-meter summit for Japan's most celebrated night panorama, the glittering hourglass of city lights pinched between two dark bays.
Goryokaku Fort and Goryokaku Tower
A star-shaped Western-style fortress from 1864, ringed by 1,500 cherry trees, best appreciated from the adjacent 107-meter tower's observation deck.
Hakodate Morning Market (Asaichi)
Steps from the station, vendors hawk glistening crab, sea urchin and squid so fresh you can fish for your own, served atop steaming donburi bowls.
Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses
Meiji-era waterfront warehouses converted into shops, beer halls and cafés glow romantically at dusk, the centerpiece of Hakodate's historic bayside district.
Motomachi District and Hachiman-zaka Slope
Cobbled slopes lined with churches and consulates plunge straight toward the harbor, with Hachiman-zaka's bay-framed view ranking among Japan's most photographed streets.
Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward
This flamboyant blue-and-yellow colonial-style hall of 1910 crowns Motomachi with chandeliered ballrooms and balcony views over the port it once governed.
Hakodate Orthodox Church
Founded by Russia's first Japanese consulate in 1859, this white Russian Byzantine church with green copper domes rings bells nicknamed 'Gan-gan-dera' across Motomachi.
Yunokawa Onsen
One of Hokkaido's oldest hot-spring resorts steams beside the sea, famous for its winter spectacle of snow monkeys soaking in the Tropical Botanical Garden's baths.
Cape Tachimachi (Tachimachi-misaki)
Dramatic sea cliffs at Mount Hakodate's southern foot overlook the Tsugaru Strait, a windswept lookout tied to poets and star-crossed local legends.
Trappistine Convent (Tenshien)
Japan's first women's Trappist monastery, founded in 1898, welcomes visitors to its red-brick Gothic buildings, rose gardens and famous nun-made butter candies.

train.note: Japan has no international trains. The Hokkaido Shinkansen runs through the undersea Seikan Tunnel from Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto station (about 20 min from central Hakodate on the Hakodate Liner) to Shin-Aomori and on toward Tokyo in roughly 4 hours in total, while JR limited-express trains run north across Hokkaido to Sapporo in about 3.5-4 hours. Note that the Shinkansen does not reach central Hakodate - the connecting Hakodate Liner shuttle is timed to each bullet train. The extension to Sapporo is still years from opening, so the Sapporo leg remains a conventional limited express.

bus.note: No international buses run from Japan. Hokkaido Bus and JR Hokkaido Bus run highway coaches from the stands outside JR Hakodate Station to Sapporo in about 5 hours, plus services to towns across southern Hokkaido; the local Hakodate Bus network and the historic tram cover the city and nearby sights. Overnight coaches to Sapporo are cheaper than the train and should be reserved by phone or at the station counter.

intl.to: Aomori (Japan) - sails from Hakodate Ferry Terminal, about 15 min by taxi north of the centre
Oma, Shimokita Peninsula (Japan) - sails from Hakodate Ferry Terminal

ferry.note: Hakodate's ferries are all domestic. Tsugaru Kaikyo Ferry sails six times daily across the strait to Aomori on Honshu in about 3 hours 40 minutes, and twice daily to Oma on the Shimokita Peninsula in around 90 minutes - the Oma boat is the shortest crossing and popular with cyclists and drivers. Seasonal sightseeing cruises operate in the bay in summer. There are no international passenger sailings, and vehicles should be booked ahead in July-August.

half.name: Onuma Quasi-National Park
half.blurb: A tranquil park of island-dotted lakes beneath the volcanic cone of Mount Komagatake, with walking and cycling paths, about 30 minutes north by train.

half.name: Mount Esan
half.blurb: An active coastal volcano with steaming vents and azalea slopes at the tip of the Kameda Peninsula, roughly an hour east of the city.

full.name: Matsumae Castle
full.blurb: Japan's northernmost traditional castle and a famous cherry-blossom town on the Tsugaru Strait, about two hours southwest of Hakodate.

full.name: Noboribetsu & Toya Onsen
full.blurb: Hokkaido's most famous hot-spring resorts, with the steaming 'Hell Valley' and the caldera lake of Toya, about 2.5-3 hours north.
